newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts Senate race has Brahmins brawling. [CORRECTED 18:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts Senate race has Brahmins brawling. [CORRECTED 18:25 GMT]

text.p: Democratic Senator John Kerry, fighting for his political life, lashed out at his Republican opponent Monday, telling Massachusetts Gov. William Weld "you talk out of both sides of your mouth more than the Budweiser frogs."
Standing on a stage in Worcester's Mechanics Hall where Mark Twain and Henry David Thoreau once spoke, Kerry and Weld sought to draw voters in the fifth of seven scheduled debates of the tight race.
Weld attacked Kerry for voting to raise the gasoline tax.

"Senator, if your name were John Sixpack instead of John Forbes Kerry, and you had to gas up your racing motorcycle and your speedboat and your airplane every weekend as well as your cars, you would have thought twice before you would have proposed raising the gas tax by 50 cents a gallon," he said.
Kerry complained about Weld's advertising campaign that has portrayed him as being soft in the war on drugs.
"It is mugging the truth ... I was a prosecutor. I spent a lifetime fighting drugs," he said.

Polls show the Senate race is a dead heat. One poll, conducted Sept 4-5 by the Boston Globe/WBZ radio, found more voters believed it was time to replace Kerry and give someone else a chance in the Senate.

Republicans are eager to re-capture the seat held by Sen. Edward Brooke until his 1978 defeat by Democrat Paul Tsongas. Tsongas chose not to run for a second term in 1984 because of health problems and Kerry was elected. (Corrects to make clear that Kerry did not win the seat from Brooke.)
The two six-foot-four millionaires with Ivy League degrees and New England blue-blood wore blue suits to Worcester, now a blue-collar city about an hour's drive west of Boston.

Kerry repeatedly took aim at Weld's cuts in education, his veto of the minimum wage and rejection of a bill that would impose a tax on cigarette companies to pay for healthcare for 165,000 children. The Democratic-controlled state legislature overrode the veto.
Weld focused on Kerry's stand against the death penalty and the Democrat's inclination to raise taxes to achieve desireable social objectives.
The governor noted that he had balanced Massachusetts' budget and carried out 11 tax cuts in the past six years.
